solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female bird, one seen in meadow

indicators.note: seen in places the bird and the one within the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
a tit is a small bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a female bird out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female bird' reads as one phrase, a hen or duck, but 'Female' alone is the definition: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a girl's name, so a female is an example of a person bearing it.

clue.text: Austrian duke takes poodle out by lake

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: out means the letters of poodle are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An Austrian nobleman walks his poodle beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'takes' and 'by' are just joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopold was the name of several Austrian dukes of the Habsburg and Babenberg lines.

clue.text: Management team thrown in river

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the river name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: thrown means the letters of team are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: The management team is pushed into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' and 'in' look like one action on the team but are two signals; the Trent is a river in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment means the handling or management of something, as of a patient or a subject.

clue.text: Carry Frenchman's tribal symbol

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is short for monsieur, the French form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A Frenchman carries an emblem of his tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: M, short for monsieur, stands for a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal revered as the emblem of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Take turns thus to get neat?

parts.note: the answer split as an instruction to change the four letters NATE says how to arrive at the word neat

explanation.surface: A suggestion that taking turns is the way to tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer as ALTER NATE, an instruction to rearrange NATE, and you get NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to occur or act by turns, one after another.

clue.text: Concession for those getting on?

parts.note: people getting on are both boarding a vehicle and growing old; a pensioner's travel card gives free rides

explanation.surface: A discount offered to passengers as they board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' means boarding and also ageing: British pensioners receive a free travel card for local buses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the free travel permit given to older people in Britain.

clue.text: Current entering fish grounds

indicators.note: entering means the symbol for current goes inside the fish word

parts.note: a bass is a fish
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electric current passes into fishing waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is electrical: I is its symbol in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are reasons or foundations, the basis for an argument or action.

clue.text: Bar work that might involve The Woolpack?

parts.note: a bar of soap
an opera is a musical work, opus being Latin for work

explanation.surface: Pub work, the sort found in a village inn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Woolpack is the village pub in the long-running British TV drama Emmerdale; 'Bar work' suggests serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running TV serial such as Emmerdale is one in which The Woolpack pub features.

clue.text: Woman in a strike at publisher's

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark telling a printer to delete, to strike out

explanation.surface: A woman caught up in a walkout at a publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action, but at a publisher's it is the instruction to strike out text, DELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a woman's first name, as borne by the singer.

clue.text: At sea it cooked stuff

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of at sea it are worked into a new mix

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, a meal was cooked and served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a noun, the thing cooked, but is the verb meaning fill up.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to fill to the point of fullness, to stuff someone with food.

clue.text: Conspicuous poverty traps

indicators.note: the word poverty traps, holds within it, the run of letters wanted

explanation.surface: Poverty traps are plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poverty traps' looks like the economic phrase, but 'traps' is the signal that the answer sits inside 'poverty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly, in plain view, so it is conspicuous.

clue.text: Witness mates, hammered, opening old wine

indicators.note: the shuffled mates go into the wine word, opening it up

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: hammered means beaten out of shape, so the letters of mates are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drunk friends broach a bottle of vintage wine as a witness looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammered' looks like slang for drunk, fitting the wine, but it is the anagram signal; 'opening' is the container signal. Tent is a little-known old wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is evidence or proof, as in a testament to someone's skill, so it bears witness.

clue.text: Exposes market's tricks

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them, so exposes gives outs
a mart is a market, and the apostrophe s gives the plural-looking form

explanation.surface: Someone reveals the dodgy practices of a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricks' looks like a noun completing 'market's tricks', but it is the verb that defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to get the better of them by cunning, which is what tricking them does.

clue.text: Old and excellent letter to Greeks

parts.note: mega is slang for excellent or great

explanation.surface: An old and fine letter sent to the people of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter to Greeks' suggests a piece of correspondence, like an epistle; it means a character of their alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter belonging to Greeks.

clue.text: Doctor West returns in vision

indicators.note: returns means the actress's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: A doctor called West comes back into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a surname or direction; it stands for the actress Mae West, whose first name 'returns' reverses to EAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a series of images seen in sleep, a vision in the night.

clue.text: Do Mark E Smith, slamming Christian outlook?

indicators.note: slamming means knocking the letters about, so they are reordered

parts.note: do is taken as written, Mark shrinks to M, its usual abbreviation, and E Smith stays as written

explanation.surface: An impression of the late singer Mark E Smith of The Fall, attacking religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark E Smith led the Manchester band The Fall; 'Mark' gives only M, and 'slamming' reorders the remaining letters into ETHODISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodism is a Protestant Christian movement, so a Christian way of seeing things; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Recipent in area with Wear feeding Dee?

indicators.note: feeding means the clothing word goes into the river name

parts.note: the Dee, a river in Scotland, Wales and England
to dress is to wear, or a dress is something to wear

explanation.surface: In a region where the River Wear flows into the River Dee, a recipient waits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear' and 'Dee' look like two British rivers, but only the Dee is a river here; Wear is clothing. 'Recipent' is a printed misspelling of recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: An addressee is the person a letter is sent to, its intended recipient.

clue.text: Monk in ANC beginning to establish control

parts.note: Dom is a title given to certain monks

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monk joins the ANC to establish power.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANC is South Africa's African National Congress, given as written; 'in' gives its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is the state of having power or control over others.

clue.text: Drunken baron also drinks here

indicators.note: drunken means unsteady, so the letters of baron also reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy aristocrat also takes his drinks in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon bar was the more comfortable lounge in a traditional British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon bar is a room in a pub, a place where people drink.

clue.text: Current setter involved in predicament

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the predicament word

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in a predicament

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of setter are mixed

explanation.surface: The setter of the puzzle is currently caught up in a tricky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' reads as one phrase, but 'involved' signals the anagram and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast, narrow current of air high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Radical adherent entertaining Mister Swan

indicators.note: entertaining means the believer word holds the swan word inside it as a guest

parts.note: a Jain is an adherent of Jainism, an Indian religion
a cob is a male swan

explanation.surface: A radical supporter plays host to a man named Swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister Swan' looks like a person; it means a male swan, COB. The Jacobins were radical French revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobin, after the French revolutionary club, has come to mean any political radical or extremist.

clue.text: Leaving south-west, migratory bird's okay

indicators.note: leaving means the compass letters depart from the bird word

parts.note: the swallow is a bird that migrates south for the winter
SW is the compass abbreviation for south-west

explanation.surface: A bird migrating away from the south-west is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s in 'bird's' is just 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something is to permit it, to give it the okay.

clue.text: One readily turns extremist joining faction

parts.note: a wing of a party is a faction within it
a nut is a fanatic or zealot

explanation.surface: A radical joins a splinter group.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a fastener with two flat flanges, which is easily turned by hand; the surface hints at the political sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing nut has projections that let it be turned by finger and thumb, so it turns readily.

clue.text: Firm embracing socialist principles

indicators.note: embracing means the company abbreviation holds the socialist word inside it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
red is a common term for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A company adopts left-wing values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective meaning steadfast principles, but it is the noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or guiding principles, from the Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Finance some men do without

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some men go without money.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow an institution is to provide it with income, to fund it.

clue.text: Less harsh one, theologian comes into metropolis

indicators.note: comes into means the pair of pieces enters the city word

parts.note: a town, a large urban place
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A gentler theologian arrives in the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the crossword's usual theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toned down has been softened or moderated, made gentler in effect.

clue.text: Great man wrests second one from painter

indicators.note: wrests means the named letter is pulled out of the painter's name

parts.note: Titian, the Venetian Renaissance painter
the second I in the painter's name, one being I

explanation.surface: A great man grabs something from an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrests' removes the second I from TITIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of great power or importance, after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Order to carry out, endlessly elaborate

parts.note: to do a task is to carry it out

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rich can mean elaborate or ornate

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry out a design, ornate without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but here it is one of the orders of classical architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture, with plain columns.

clue.text: Black dominant on move in game

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: on the move means the letters of dominant are shifted around

explanation.surface: A chess commentary: Black has the upper hand and it is their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on move' rearranges DOMINANT into ADMINTON; the surface misleads towards chess with Black to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, so it is a game.

clue.text: Day was one men brought back skip

indicators.note: brought back means the letters for men are turned round

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for enlisted men
a skip is a large waste container, a bin

explanation.surface: On that day, one of the men returned to jump about.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robin Day was a famous British television interviewer, so 'Day' was a Robin. A skip in Britain is a large builders' rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcaster Sir Robin Day bore this first name, so Day was an example of one.

clue.text: Reformed character receiving second journalist

indicators.note: receiving means the abbreviation for second goes inside the phrase for a reformed person

parts.note: a reformed character is a new man

explanation.surface: A changed person takes on a reporter as an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like an anagram signal on 'character', but the two words together mean a new man.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a reporter or journalist who gathers and writes the news.

clue.text: Piece of work runs into bar

indicators.note: into means the cricket abbreviation goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in all bar one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A section of writing hits a snag at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub or rod but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is an extract, a passage taken from a longer piece of writing or music.
